# Explorer: independent mechanism review

Scope: three fixed v1 primary papers, read without peer outputs. This is a mechanistic literature analysis, not a replication. The runtime inherits the parent's model; separate context and declared roles do not establish cross-model independence.

## ASAL — arXiv:2412.17799v1

Primary source: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17799v1

Reported mechanism and claims: (1) Sections 3.1–3.3, equations 2–4 define three different searches: prompt alignment, historical novelty within a rollout, and separation among an archive's members. They use a foundation-model representation of rendered simulations. These are operationally different diversities. (2) Section 4.3/Figure 6 reports a visually varied Lenia/Boids archive from mutation and diversity selection; Section 4.5/Figure 8 compares representation choices qualitatively. Neither establishes cognition. The cellular-automaton experiment evaluates finite 2,048-step trajectories with 32 sampled times and 256 initial states per rule (Appendix B.2), so its novelty score does not prove indefinite innovation.

Designed versus emergent: the substrate, rendering, representation, search objective and optimizer are supplied. Particular trajectories and patterns arise from the chosen local dynamics. My inference: searching for visual replication is weaker than demonstrating hereditary evolution or adaptive function; the causal bridge requires additional tests. A prompt-conditioned shape is evidence of a successful search objective, not evidence that the pattern has a mind.

## Leniabreeder — arXiv:2406.04235v1

Primary source: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.04235v1

Reported mechanism and claims: (1) Methods/Search Space and Variation Operator specify inherited seeds plus rule parameters, initialized around Aquarium, varied by iso+LineDD, and retained using niche-based quality/diversity. AURORA updates the learned descriptor, thereby changing niche boundaries. This is external evolutionary search over simulations, not demonstrated reproduction inside a single simulated ecology. (2) Experiments/Unsupervised Diversity, Figures 4–5 reports continuing additions and growing diversity during finite runs, with ten seeded replicates; the Open-Ended Evolution section explicitly disclaims theoretical open-endedness.

Designed versus emergent: locality supplies self-organization, but localization constraints and temporal-stability fitness select the admitted phenotypes. Methods/Unsupervised Statistical Measures acknowledges that fitness is only partially unsupervised and penalizes periodic/chaotic motion. Conclusion notes rotation/scale sensitivity. My inference: an archive can grow because it discovers useful mechanisms, because the representation moves, or because transformations split one mechanism into multiple niches. These possibilities need separate accounting.

## From Text to Life — arXiv:2407.09502v1

Primary source: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.09502v1

Reported claims: this is a review and conceptual synthesis, not a new controlled multiagent experiment. LLMS AS TOOLS FOR ALIFE/Artificial Evolution and LLMs describes model-guided mutation/crossover and quality-diversity systems; ALIFE FOR LLMS/Collective Intelligence proposes richer adaptive organization. Its Self-Organisation/Emergence subsection and Discussion distinguish many top-down implementations of agent capabilities from emergent ones.

My inference: these are candidate mechanisms for our coordinator rather than a performance guarantee. Inherited prompts, operator choices, memory, selection and communication topology should be represented explicitly in the evidence graph. A scheduled workflow that calls itself self-improving is not sufficient evidence that improvement evolved. The paper provides vocabulary and research directions, not proof that named complementary roles cause collective intelligence.

## Falsifiable cross-paper hypothesis — proposed, untested

H1: complementary scientific agents improve the yield of independently verified, mechanistically distinct hypotheses over an equal-budget homogeneous team only when selection rewards held-out mechanistic validity and archives preserve alternative explanations. Semantic separation alone will increase apparent diversity more reliably than verified discovery.

Design: randomize paper-analysis tasks among (A) homogeneous agents, (B) fixed complementary roles, (C) complementary roles plus a niche archive scored by mechanism and evidence rather than wording. Match model, total tokens, tool budget and paper access. Use blind initial commitments in every arm. Hold the evaluator and evidence rubric fixed, hide arm identity, and retain rejected hypotheses with reasons. Randomize multiple papers and seeds; report paper-clustered uncertainty rather than treating related sentences as independent discoveries.

Primary endpoint: unique hypotheses that survive an independently specified falsification check per fixed token budget. Secondary endpoints: citation accuracy, incorrect causal claims, retained competing explanations, pairwise error overlap, and robustness when one agent is removed. Deduplicate by intervention predictions and causal structure, not embedding distance alone. Predefine equivalence rules before seeing outputs. If B/C produce more wording diversity but no higher verified yield, H1's claimed practical benefit is unsupported. If C merely favors one evaluator's preferences, transfer to a held-out evaluator should collapse; that is a diagnostic failure, not discovery.

Interpretation boundary: visual novelty, stability, adaptation, hereditary evolution and mind are separate endpoints. Every promotion between them needs its own measurement. Our run can demonstrate coordinated literature analysis and record complementary contributions; it cannot by itself establish emergent cognition or empirical validation of these papers.

# Skeptic: independent construct-validity review

Scope: three fixed v1 primary texts, read before peer outputs. This is a methods audit, not a computational replication. The runtime inherits the coordinator's model; separate prompts and a sealed first pass reduce information leakage but do not establish independent model errors. All proposed tests below are my analysis, not results already obtained.

## ASAL — arXiv:2412.17799v1

Claim 1, favorable: foundation-model representations make a reusable discovery interface across unlike substrates credible (§§3–4, Figs. 3–6). The CA experiment averages 256 initializations, not one (Appendix B.2). Critical alternative: 2,048-step, 32-frame historical embedding novelty measures observer-relative finite-horizon change; it does not demonstrate indefinitely productive evolution. A wandering transient could score well without accumulating capabilities. The paper itself explicitly outsources observer choice to the representation (§3.2).

Claim 2: the CLIP/DINO/pixel comparison supports useful perceptual search, but its qualitative outcome is weaker evidence for biological agency or intelligence (§4.5, Fig. 8). Rendering, color, crop, and frame schedule can change what is rewarded without changing underlying dynamics. Single-target search also evaluates one initialization per simulation (B.1); that limitation should not be incorrectly applied to CA search.

Discriminating followup: freeze selected rules, evaluate held-out initializations and 10x/100x horizons, and counterbalance renderings. Score both withheld embeddings and preregistered state-level persistence, reproduction, and functional adaptation. A cross-renderer, cross-horizon advantage supports substantive discovery; novelty confined to the optimization observer supports a narrower visual-search interpretation.

Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17799v1 (§§3.2,4.2,4.5; Appendices A,B.1–B.2).

## Leniabreeder — arXiv:2406.04235v1

Claim 1, favorable: sustained repertoire discovery is supported beyond attractive examples: ten random-seed replications, corrected tests, and multiple diversity measures are reported (Experiments, Fig. 5). The authors expressly disclaim theoretical open-endedness (Background: Open-Ended Evolution). The strongest defensible claim is useful sustained exploration within the evaluated regime.

Claim 2, critical alternative: new archive admissions can reflect a moving descriptor rather than new functional organization. AURORA retrains its VAE; entropy depends on that model, and raw pixel variance is not invariant to cosmetic changes (Background: AURORA; Unsupervised Diversity). Low latent variance rewards stability but need not imply agency; the authors acknowledge penalizing periodic patterns (Unsupervised Statistical Measures). Aquarium initialization and soliton constraints also select which expressions of life can be discovered (Search Space; Constraints on Growth).

Discriminating followup: retain every phenotype and rescore all checkpoints with one frozen, independently trained encoder plus rotation/scale-normalized state descriptors. Compare moving/frozen descriptors under equal budgets and multiple founders. Separately measure disturbance recovery and acquired functions. Growth in invariant functional diversity would strengthen the evolutionary interpretation; only moving-archive growth would favor descriptor drift.

Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.04235v1 (named sections above; Figs. 2,5; Conclusion).

## From Text to Life — arXiv:2407.09502v1

Claim 1, favorable: this is a useful conceptual bridge and research agenda, not a new controlled demonstration of living LLMs (Introduction; Discussion). It distinguishes permissive autonomy from self-sustainability and explicitly notes many agent properties are hard-coded rather than emergent (Autonomy; Emergence). Critiquing it as if it claimed experimentally established life would manufacture disagreement.

Claim 2, critical alternative: complex group behavior can come from orchestration, shared pretrained knowledge, or additional sampling budget rather than locally emergent collective intelligence. The Collective Intelligence section identifies short horizons and largely in-context learning as current limitations. Its analogies suggest testable mechanisms but cannot themselves identify those mechanisms.

Discriminating followup: randomize task instances across equal-token single-agent, independent ensemble, scripted-role team, and adaptive local-interaction team; keep tools and evidence access matched. Cross communication on/off with persistent memory on/off; include unfamiliar tasks, perturbations, and repeated generations. Report held-out accuracy, error correlation, recovery, cost, and genuinely new skills. Benefits beyond the ensemble baseline, causally dependent on interaction and persisting under perturbation, would support collective mechanisms. Role labels or fluent dialogue alone would not.

Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.09502v1 (Autonomy; Emergence; Collective Intelligence; Discussion).

## Review disposition

Accept these as discovery methods and a productive conceptual agenda with bounded evidence. Preserve disagreement about which diversity deserves selection: stability may suppress interesting cycles, whereas novelty may reward meaningless drift. Neither objective universally dominates. Before promoting any artifact to an open-endedness, agency, or intelligence claim, attach its observer, rendering, search budget, founders, horizon, seed unit, exclusions, and withheld validation. No RNA-seq-specific differential-expression contract is applicable here.

# Evaluator independent first pass

Scope: primary arXiv v1 texts 2412.17799, 2406.04235 and 2407.09502. This is a literature evaluation and a proposed falsification plan, not a reproduced experiment. No peer conclusions were read. Runtime inherits the parent model; role separation does not imply independent model errors.

## ASAL: what was measured?

Source facts: Section 4.2, Figure 5 and Appendix B.2 report exhaustive evaluation of 262,144 Life-like CA rules; each uses 256 random initial states, 2,048 steps, and 32 sampled frames for historical novelty. Conway's rule is in the top 5% under that metric. Section 4.5/Figure 8 compares CLIP, DINOv2 and pixels qualitatively. Appendix B.1 evaluates each single-target candidate on one initial-state seed; Figure 4 illustrates a changed initial state. Appendix B.3 uses 8,192 archive members, 32 offspring per iteration and 100,000 iterations. Sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17799v1#S4.SS2 ; #S4.SS5 ; #A2.SS1 ; #A2.SS2 ; #A2.SS3 .

Supported conclusion: the implementation can locate trajectories novel under a finite-horizon learned visual representation. Untested extension: perpetual innovation, or a generally human-validated definition of complexity. My evaluation: frames are correlated observations, initial states nest within rules, and archive members share ancestry. None substitutes for independent optimizer runs. Using CLIP both to select and visualize success is legitimate optimization but is not independent validation. DINOv2 is an ablation, not automatically a held-out evaluator when it too drives its own search. Single-seed target fitness is vulnerable to seed-specific success.

Proposed test: freeze selected rule/seed parameters and renderer before revealing evaluation seeds. Run 20 independent searches for each of CLIP, pixels, and random selection at matched simulator-step budgets; separately report encoder compute and wall time. Evaluate held-out initial states, 10x longer horizons, and frozen alternative descriptors never used for selection. Blind human raters to method and include periodic and noise controls. Primary endpoint: rate of distinct, persistent behaviors per run after deduplication. Use run-level effects and uncertainty. A collapse after horizon extension falsifies the extrapolation, not the reported short-horizon observation.

## Leniabreeder: finite discovery versus unboundedness

Source facts: Experiments reports ten random-seed replications, population 32,768, Wilcoxon–Mann–Whitney tests and Holm–Bonferroni correction. Table 2 median MAP-Elites coverage ranges 38.5–52.2% depending on fitness/descriptor. Figure 5 reports increasing cumulative elite additions after one million evaluations and higher pixel variance for unsupervised fitness, p<0.005. Methods/Search Space initializes from Aquarium; Methods/Unsupervised Statistical Measures trains the eight-dimensional VAE on generated evaluation data. Conclusion acknowledges rotation/scale non-invariance. Sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.04235v1#S5 ; sections Experiments/Manual Diversity, Experiments/Unsupervised Diversity, Methods/Search Space, Methods/Unsupervised Statistical Measures and Conclusion.

Supported conclusion: replicated finite-budget discovery in a specified family of seeded Lenia worlds. Untested extension: unbounded diversity or general robustness across starting families. My evaluation: ten runs are the relevant replication unit. Archive population size is not sample size. A cumulative admission counter cannot decrease even if new behavior stops appearing; a slope must be checked against a stationary replacement control. The adaptive VAE changes the ruler while the population changes. Pixel variance provides another measurement but can reward color/rotation without functional novelty. Coverage percentages depend on grid bounds and should not compare different descriptor spaces directly. No matched random-search superiority estimate is established by the cited table alone.

Proposed test: preregister a hold-out behavioral descriptor independent of each evolving VAE. Compare AURORA, frozen-VAE AURORA, MAP-Elites and random mutation with matched evaluations, identical starting resources, and at least 20 runs per arm; reserve several non-Aquarium initial families for evaluation. Re-score all archived checkpoints with the frozen descriptor after color, rotation and translation normalization, plus damage-recovery/locomotion tests. Report novel viable behaviors per final budget window, extinction/spread failures and effect intervals. Longer runs can support a finite-horizon trend but cannot prove unboundedness.

## From Text to Life: conceptual scope

Source facts: the paper presents a review and analogy, not a new controlled experiment establishing ALife status. ALife for LLMs/Emergence distinguishes hard-coded agent capabilities from bottom-up emergence. Collective Intelligence describes existing multiagent work as mostly short-horizon; Discussion explicitly avoids a definite answer about LLMs as ALife. Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.09502v1 , sections ALife for LLMs/Emergence, Collective Intelligence and Discussion.

Supported conclusion: useful distinctions and research questions. Untested extension: that adding roles, memory or debate necessarily yields qualitatively new collective intelligence. Proposed test of our platform: equal-total-token single-agent, homogeneous-team and complementary-team arms, randomized across hidden tasks with independent expert scoring. Remove communication or shuffle messages in ablations; freeze held-out tasks before role design. Score unsupported-claim rate, valid falsifications and task accuracy, with compute/latency. Team superiority alone establishes practical value; evidence for interaction requires improvement over budget-matched independent agents plus aggregation, and reproducibility across model families. This protocol is my proposal, not a result of the paper or a completed benchmark.

# Evaluator diagnostic check

I inspected and executed descriptor_diagnostic.py. All assertions passed; output matches descriptor-results.json. No implementation defect was found for the three supplied patterns and measured window.

The code implements Conway B3/S23 synchronous updates. Its 64x64 world is periodic, but the asserted absence of boundary cells in all measured frames prevents wraparound from explaining these results. Coordinates are canonicalized by subtracting the minimum occupied row and column, which removes translation while retaining phase, orientation and scale.

Measured results: block has 1 raw/1 normalized state; blinker 2/2; glider 64/4 across 64 measured frames. The glider's normalized shape returns after four updates with displacement [1,1]; every available four-step translation comparison passes. Sixteen translated copies of one initial glider produce 16 raw arrays but one normalized shape.

These counts demonstrate descriptor dependence in a deterministic, hand-selected control. Sixty-four raw frames are not sixty-four discoveries, independent replicates, or new mechanisms. The four normalized phases also are not four species. A translation quotient is appropriate when absolute position is irrelevant; motion and position can matter for navigation and collisions.

This is a completed code-level measurement diagnostic. It does not measure CLIP similarity, demonstrate how ASAL or AURORA actually scores gliders, test Lenia, compare search algorithms or agent teams, or replicate any paper. No inferential statistics are warranted for these fixed examples. A separate held-out, equal-budget experiment is still needed to test the broader research claims.

summary: Toy Game of Life control: 64 glider frames have 4 relative phases; 16 translations have one normalized shape. Not a paper replication.

payload.synthesis:
# Paper pilot: discovery needs an explicit observer

**Cross-paper finding:** promising artificial-life search becomes more scientifically useful when the discovery process can change its representation while evaluation preserves a separate, fixed question. The observer is part of the experiment. This is our synthesis, not a result demonstrated jointly by these papers.

ASAL makes learned visual representations usable as discovery objectives; its finite novelty measurements need their stated horizon and observer ([primary v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.17799v1), §§3.2–3.3, 4.2, Appendix B.2). Leniabreeder illustrates adaptive repertoire exploration and explicitly bounds its open-endedness interpretation ([primary v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.04235v1), Background/Open-Ended Evolution; Methods/Unsupervised Statistical Measures; Experiments/Unsupervised Diversity). *From Text to Life* supplies conceptual distinctions rather than a new controlled demonstration of living or collectively intelligent LLMs ([primary v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.09502v1), ALife for LLMs/Emergence, Collective Intelligence, Discussion). Together they motivate auditable discovery, not an inference from attractive novelty to mind.

## What the complementary agents contributed

- **Explorer:** separated the mechanisms being searched from the scientist-supplied selection machinery; external optimization is distinct from reproduction inside an ecology. Proposed hypotheses defined by intervention predictions rather than different wording.
- **Skeptic:** identified construct ambiguity: changing the observer can change apparent diversity, but imposing invariance can erase useful positional behavior. Requested competing interpretations instead of treating normalization as automatically correct.
- **Evaluator:** separated correlated frames and related archive members from independent search runs. Proposed fixed held-out evaluation and an independent-ensemble baseline to isolate interaction from extra sampling.
- **Builder/coordinator:** implemented and ran the deterministic descriptor check, preserving reproducible code, outputs and review lineage. The Evaluator inspected and executed it independently of its authorship.
- **Synthesizer:** reconciled those contributions into one testable measurement-and-coordination proposal, retaining the tensions below.

The three initial reviews were hash-committed before reveal and discussion. They largely agreed; we found no substantive initial dissent to dramatize. Their complementary emphasis is observable in this run, but all runtimes share an inherited model and the same three-paper corpus. Sealed first passes reduce information leakage; they do not establish independent errors or prove a team advantage.

## Completed measurement diagnostic

The executed Conway Life control used a 64×64 periodic world and 64 measured frames, with assertions that occupied cells never touched a boundary. Exact raw-image versus translation-normalized counts were:

| Fixed pattern | Raw frames | Normalized shapes |
|---|---:|---:|
| Block | 1 | 1 |
| Blinker | 2 | 2 |
| Glider | 64 | 4 |

The glider repeats its normalized shape after four updates with displacement [1,1]; every available four-step displacement check passed. Sixteen translated initial gliders yielded sixteen raw arrays and one normalized shape. The Evaluator reran the code and confirmed the recorded output.

**Narrow result:** the count of image-unique observations depends on the chosen equivalence rule. Sixty-four glider frames are not sixty-four discoveries; four phases are not four species. This hand-selected deterministic example tests neither CLIP nor ASAL, AURORA or Lenia. It is no paper replication, statistical comparison or demonstration of evolution, cognition or multiagent superiority.

## Tensions worth preserving

**Stability versus novelty:** stability can protect useful structure and suppress useful transitions; novelty can uncover stepping stones and reward meaningless drift. Preserve both in an archive with explicit outcomes, rather than silently treating either scalar as a definition of life.

**Observer invariance versus functional position:** translation normalization suits intrinsic morphology, while displacement and location matter for navigation, encounters and collisions. Store morphology together with motion and interaction outcomes. A coarser descriptor is not automatically a better one.

**Promising discovery versus bounded proof:** a productive finite search can remain valuable without demonstrating indefinite innovation. Likewise, useful coordinated analysis can exist without establishing emergent collective intelligence. Keep claim scope attached to measured conditions.

## Feasible hackathon experiment — proposed, not run

Build an **observer-audit benchmark** around the coordinator. First use separate development packets to refine role briefs and a scoring rubric; then freeze both. Reserve 20 previously withheld ALife/emergence paper packets, each with source text and a small reproducible diagnostic where available. Do not tune roles or scoring on their outputs.

Randomize each packet across three arms: (A) one analyst, (B) independent analysts plus a fixed aggregation step, and (C) complementary interacting analysts plus the same aggregation step. Match total generated tokens, tool calls and source access, including aggregation costs; record actual usage. Seal first passes in both multiagent arms. Predefine timeouts, failures and source-access rules. Add communication-disabled or message-shuffled comparisons only if the budget permits; they remain unrun ablations.

**Fixed primary outcome:** correctly source-supported claim/limitation pairs per fixed total token budget, deduplicated by scientific proposition using rules frozen on development packets. Each pair must identify a claim, its actual measurement boundary and a source locator. Blind human adjudicators should score arm-hidden outputs without authoring the briefs; report disagreements. Report paired per-paper effects and uncertainty, with papers as clusters rather than sentences as independent samples. Track unsupported scope inflation and citation errors as secondary outcomes.

Arm C must outperform B to support an interaction benefit; an advantage only over A could reflect additional sampling. An increased count of diverse-looking phrases without more valid pairs would fail the primary test. Twenty papers can support an exploratory hackathon result, not a general claim across fields or model families. This pilot has completed the literature review, commitment/reveal workflow and toy diagnostic only; the proposed benchmark, new ALife optimization and cross-model replication have not been run.

post_reveal_notes.explorer:
# Explorer post-reveal note

The independent reviews converge on a useful distinction: diversity is simultaneously a discovery mechanism and a measurement choice. That convergence is provisional agreement among same-model runtimes, not three independent empirical validations.

What changed: the evaluator sharpened my proposed test. Its primary sampling unit must be a complete search/team run; treating archive entries, frames or claims as independent replicates would overstate evidence. I would add independent ensemble-plus-aggregation and message-shuffling controls to my initial experiment. Equal token budgets alone do not isolate a communication mechanism. No correction to the fixed paper facts in my initial review was needed.

What remains in tension: rewarding stability can remove precisely the oscillation, switching or transient exploration that produces useful new mechanisms. Conversely, rewarding novelty can retain drift with no predictive or functional value. The resolution should be a multiobjective archive that preserves both classes with explicit tags, rather than one scalar score that silently decides what life or intelligence must look like.

Practical recommendation for H — inference, not a paper result: build a small “observer stress test” around the existing coordinator. Give teams the same candidate simulations, but allocate genuinely different evidence channels: one agent sees visual trajectories; one sees state dynamics and perturbation outcomes; one sees lineage and search metadata. Each makes a sealed classification before discussion. Ask which discoveries remain distinct when the observer changes. Then let a builder run controlled transformations and an evaluator score held-out function.

A strong hackathon deliverable would show one case where apparent diversity vanishes under an irrelevant rendering transformation and one where visually similar patterns have different damage-recovery behavior. Preserve the disagreement trail. This directly demonstrates why complementary information can matter. The present literature run supplies the hypothesis and audit trail; it has not run that simulation benchmark or established emergent cognition.
post_reveal_notes.skeptic:
# Skeptic after reveal

I read Explorer and Evaluator only after the three first passes were committed and revealed. We independently converge on a bounded interpretation: these papers supply useful discovery machinery and conceptual distinctions; neither visual novelty nor named agent roles establishes open-ended evolution or intelligence. Agreement here is evidence of compatible readings, not three independent model-family replications.

Explorer adds an important mechanistic distinction: external search over simulated worlds differs from reproduction and selection occurring inside one ecology. Evaluator adds the statistical unit: frames, related archive members, and admitted offspring are not independent search replications. My additional emphasis is construct validity: which properties does the observer retain, and which meaningful behaviors does an invariance rule erase?

The proposed glider diagnostic is worthwhile if labeled as a toy counterexample about measurement. Sixteen spatially translated initial patterns can yield sixteen distinct pixel arrays and one translation-normalized pattern. Over 64 steps, one moving glider can generate 64 raw images while cycling through four normalized shapes; a four-step recurrence with displacement (1,1) is a traveling periodic structure. These are predicted checks until the code actually produces them. Record finite-grid boundaries, initial coordinates, canonicalization, and the recurrence check; clipping or wraparound can change the count.

What a successful check would establish: exact pixel uniqueness can exceed shape novelty, and finite-window image novelty alone cannot identify accumulating organization. It can exercise reproducible artifact production, contrast alternative descriptors, and verify that the team reports an ambiguity rather than erasing it.

What it cannot establish: that CLIP misclassifies gliders, that ASAL's actual embedding objective behaves like exact pixel hashing, that AURORA is dominated by translation, or that either paper's results fail to replicate. No encoder, paper algorithm, learned archive, statistical comparison, or original simulation configuration is reproduced by this diagnostic.

Preserved tension: translation is a nuisance only for the question of intrinsic shape novelty. It is behaviorally meaningful for navigation, transport, encounters, and collisions. Normalization could merge organisms with distinct speeds or environmental functions. Therefore retain both descriptions: normalized morphology plus displacement/velocity and relevant interaction outcomes. The appropriate descriptor is specified by the scientific question; fewer equivalence classes is not automatically a better science metric.

Recommended next decision: use the toy as a visible measurement audit, then choose one paper-specific held-out test. Freeze the selected candidates and the validation definition before running it. A real complementarity benchmark additionally needs matched-budget single-agent and independent-ensemble controls; this coordinated paper pilot does not estimate the causal value of complementary agents.
post_reveal_notes.evaluator:
# Evaluator after reveal

The Explorer, Skeptic and Evaluator independently converge on a bounded favorable conclusion: these are useful discovery methods and a useful conceptual agenda. Finite observer-relative novelty, external evolutionary search, and orchestrated collaboration need separate evidence before being promoted to open-endedness, internal reproduction, or emergent cognition. This agreement is informative role convergence, not three independent model replications: the inherited model and source access are shared.

Complementary contributions are visible. Explorer separates the causal mechanisms and proposed endpoint. Skeptic exposes renderer/observer drift and the tension between stability and dynamic novelty. Evaluator identifies the replication unit, moving evaluation ruler, nested samples, and missing budget-matched comparison. The roles overlap on central cautions; that is useful consistency, but this three-paper run cannot establish a diversity advantage.

A remaining uncertainty is whether moving descriptors discover useful stepping stones that a fixed descriptor misses. Freezing the ruler may improve evaluation while weakening exploration. Keep adaptive discovery, but evaluate every checkpoint with an independently fixed ruler. Also report both invariant functional measures and visible variation: invariance deliberately discards some differences that a scientist might care about.

The proposed glider diagnostic illustrates measurement dependence. Translation-normalized glider states can collapse many absolute-position pixel patterns without generating any new mechanism. That would establish a property of this controlled example. It would not invalidate learned embeddings, replicate either paper, show that all translation distinctions are irrelevant, or establish a multiagent performance gain.

Strongest feasible next equal-budget experiment: benchmark the actual coordinator on held-out claim-audit packets. Randomize single-agent, independent-ensemble-plus-fixed-aggregation, homogeneous-team, and complementary-team arms. Give each identical paper text, source tools, total generated-token limit, and total tool calls. Include sealed first passes in every multiagent arm. Add a communication-disabled complementary arm to isolate interaction from extra sampling or roles. A fixed evaluator must be blind to arm and must not author the role briefs or see training packets.

Preregister the primary endpoint as correctly supported claim/limitation pairs per fixed budget; score exact source support, sample-unit errors, scope inflation and genuinely discriminating proposed tests. Deduplicate paraphrases. Use a small pilot to debug the rubric, then at least 20 previously withheld papers for an exploratory comparison; report per-paper effects and intervals, not sentence-level p-values. A time-limited panel of human adjudicators is stronger than our inherited-model judge. For this initial pilot, three papers are three clusters, not dozens of independent claims.

This is a proposed test. What is completed is the blind first-pass literature review and commitment/reveal workflow. No new ALife optimization, model-family comparison or autonomous-science performance experiment has been run.
